job.title: Electrical Reliability Engineer
job.description:
About the role:

An opportunity exists for an experienced Electrical Reliability Engineer to join a major mining operator’s Cloudbreak OPF Engineering & Reliability team. This role will focus on improving the reliability, availability and performance of electrical assets across a large-scale operating processing plant, with a strong emphasis on reducing recurring equipment failures and transitioning from reactive breakdown maintenance to proactive, preventative maintenance strategies.

You will be responsible for investigating electrical failure modes, developing maintenance strategies and implementing practical engineering solutions to improve long-term asset performance. This is a predominantly reliability-focused position, with approximately 80% reliability engineering and 20% site support, project and design activities.
  • Initial 6-month contract based at Cloudbreak, WA, with potential for extension
  • $65/hr + super, with flexibility for the right candidate
  • 8:6 FIFO roster, site-based position
  • Focus on electrical reliability, preventative maintenance and defect elimination
  • Work across motors, VSDs, MCCs, transformers, switchboards and processing plant infrastructure
  • Opportunity to make a direct impact on plant availability, maintenance costs and operational performance

What you’ll be doing:
  • Provide electrical engineering and reliability support across the operating processing plant
  • Investigate recurring electrical equipment failures and identify opportunities to improve asset performance
  • Apply Root Cause Analysis (RCA), FMEA/FMECA and defect elimination methodologies
  • Develop and optimise preventative, predictive and periodic maintenance strategies
  • Identify bad-actor equipment and implement practical solutions to prevent recurring failures
  • Review maintenance plans, equipment criticality and condition monitoring requirements
  • Support reliability improvement initiatives across motors, VSDs, MCCs, transformers and switchrooms
  • Provide engineering support across LV distribution systems, 415V and 690V equipment, with exposure to higher-voltage systems
  • Develop scopes of work, Bills of Materials (BOMs) and technical engineering documentation
  • Support minor electrical projects, design reviews, commissioning and operational requirements
  • Collaborate with maintenance, operations, engineering and project teams to improve plant reliability
  • Identify opportunities to reduce equipment downtime, maintenance costs and reactive breakdown work
What you’ll need to be successful in the role:
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • Demonstrated experience as an Electrical Engineer within mining, mineral processing, heavy industry, oil & gas or manufacturing
  • Strong experience in electrical reliability and maintenance engineering
  • Experience developing and improving preventative or periodic maintenance strategies
  • Proven ability to investigate recurring electrical failures and implement long-term solutions
  • Understanding of Root Cause Analysis (RCA), FMEA/FMECA and defect elimination
  • Experience with LV electrical systems, particularly 415V and/or 690V
  • Experience working with motors, VSDs/VFDs, MCCs, transformers, switchboards and associated electrical equipment
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • Experience developing engineering scopes of work and technical documentation
  • Working knowledge of relevant Australian Standards and commercial electrical systems
  • Current WA C-Class Driver’s Licence
  • Strong communication, planning and stakeholder management skills
  • Mining or mineral processing experience highly regarded, particularly within iron ore or fixed plant environments
  • Exposure to 11kV, 22kV and/or 33kV systems, condition monitoring, CMMS/SAP or reliability-centred maintenance (RCM) advantageous
  • Instrumentation, PLC, HV switching and commissioning experience advantageous
How to Apply:

If this opportunity sounds interesting, please click apply or email your CV directly to me at ryan@versegroup.com.au.

For further details or enquiries, feel free to reach out directly via email or call on 0468 099 638.

job.title: RF Specialist, Emergency Services
job.description:
About the role:
We’re looking for an experienced Microwave and RF Engineer to join a highly technical communications environment supporting critical P25 radio networks across the Victorian Metropolitan Mobile Radio (MMR) and Regional Mobile Radio (RMR) networks.
  
This role will provide specialist RF technical expertise across the operations, maintenance, engineering and upgrade of complex radio systems, microwave links and associated telecommunications infrastructure. You’ll support, triage and reconfigure live links, run coverage predictions, and act as the escalation point for Network Operations and Field Engineering teams. Tower and installation work is handled by riggers, so your focus is design, configuration and operational support.
  
This suits an engineer who has designed microwave links and supported them in live operations, and who understands microwave as a digital system built on radio principles at higher frequency.
  • Permanent, full-time role based in Melbourne
  • Up to $135,000 + Super, depending on skill and experience
  • Join a global leader in mission-critical communications and public safety technology, offering the stability and scale of an established multinational alongside genuinely meaningful work
  • Clear pathway to Senior Engineering Specialist / Design Authority
  • 24x7 on-call roster with minimal ad hoc travel to metro sites
What You’ll Be Doing:
  • Provide operational support, maintenance and technical escalation for microwave links and transmission infrastructure supporting P25 networks across Victoria.
  • Act as the RF SME, supporting RF coverage, propagation, microwave links and network performance.
  • Manage network-level configuration across mixed fibre and microwave transmission feeding multiple systems.
  • Investigate and resolve complex RF and network performance issues, working with NOC, Field Engineering and vendors.
  • Support network testing, integration, upgrades and ongoing improvements across radio and transmission infrastructure.
  • Conduct RF measurements, coverage analysis and propagation modelling to ensure network performance and reliability.
  • Design RF site configurations, applying deep technical knowledge of antenna systems, propagation characteristics and site-specific nuances to deliver optimal network performance.
  • Conduct site surveys and spectrum analysis using industry-standard survey tools and spectrum analysers to assess RF conditions and identify potential interference.
  • Perform coverage prediction, modelling and calculations to inform network design and validate performance against real-world survey measurements.
  • Prepare clear technical reports covering performance, surveys and design recommendations.
  • Support core network infrastructure including firewalls, routers, switches, microwave links, and physical/virtual servers, both remotely and onsite.
  • Develop and maintain as-built documentation, change and problem management procedures, and test protocols. 
What You’ll Need to Be Successful:
  • Full Australian working rights
  • Tertiary Engineering qualification or strong equivalent industry experience.
  • Hands-on operational experience with microwave systems, supporting, programming, triaging and reconfiguring them (Aviat preferred, other vendors considered).
  • Experience designing microwave links and supporting them in live operations.
  • Microwave coverage prediction and modelling experience.
  • Strong understanding of microwave as digital systems operating on radio principles at higher frequency.
  • Network-level configuration experience in a mixed transmission environment, not microwave in isolation.
  • Strong report writing and documentation skills.
  • Australian driver’s licence, willingness to travel to metro + remote sites and participate in a 24x7 on-call roster.
Highly Regarded:
  • LMR or P25 system experience (Motorola experience not required)
  • RF survey tools and spectrum test equipment experience
  • Knowledge of TSB-88 and ACMA spectrum licensing
How to Apply:
If this sounds like your kind of role, I’d love to hear from you. Click Apply or send your CV to addison@versegroup.com.au and let’s have a chat about the opportunity and what’s next!!

job.title: Study Lead
job.description:

Working across the early stages of the digital project lifecycle, you’ll play a key role in framing business problems, assessing potential solutions, evaluating technology options and developing recommendations to support investment and delivery decisions.
  
About the Role:
  • Lead digital studies from initial opportunity identification through to solution assessment and recommendations.
  • Work with business and operational stakeholders to understand challenges, define problems and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Develop business cases, assess commercial considerations and support investment decisions.
  • Conduct options analysis, including buy-versus-build assessments and evaluations of potential technology solutions.
  • Research technology providers, assess vendor offerings and identify suitable solutions to meet business needs.
  • Facilitate workshops and discussions to challenge existing processes and explore alternative approaches.
  • Support the development of high-level solution designs, detailed requirements and proof-of-value activities.
  • Assess the feasibility, benefits, risks and potential business impact of proposed solutions.

About You
  • You’re a commercially minded and strategic thinker who can work across business and technology, challenge conventional approaches and turn complex problems into practical recommendations.

  • Experience developing business cases, conducting options analysis and evaluating technology solutions.

job.title: Graduate IT Support
job.description:

This is a fantastic opportunity for recent IT graduates looking to get their foot in the door and build a long-term career in technology.
 
Unlike some entry-level IT roles where you might be limited to repetitive tasks, working within an MSP provides exposure to a broad range of clients, technologies and technical challenges.

You'll work alongside experienced IT professionals, develop practical troubleshooting skills and gain valuable hands-on experience across modern business technology environments.

Most importantly, our client is hiring for attitude and potential, not years of technical experience.
 
The Role
As a Graduate IT Support Engineer, you'll be part of a team delivering technical support to a diverse range of business customers.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing Level 1 IT support to customers via phone, email and remote support tools.
  • Troubleshooting hardware, software, network and connectivity issues.
  • Assisting with Microsoft 365, Windows and general desktop support.
  • Logging, managing and resolving support tickets.
  • Escalating more complex technical issues to senior engineers.
  • Assisting with workstation setups, user onboarding and IT deployments.
  • Building positive relationships with customers through excellent service.
  • Developing your technical knowledge through hands-on experience and guidance from experienced colleagues.
About You
 
We're looking for two bright, personable and motivated graduates who are genuinely excited about starting a career in IT.
 
You'll ideally have:
  • Recently completed, or be close to completing, an IT-related university degree, diploma or TAFE qualification.
  • Previous customer-facing employment experience while studying, ideally in hospitality, retail or a similar service environment.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • A positive attitude, strong work ethic and willingness to learn.
  • Confidence speaking with customers and helping solve problems.
  • A genuine interest in technology and troubleshooting.
  • Basic knowledge of Windows, Microsoft 365, networking or IT support fundamentals.
  • The ability to work collaboratively and take ownership of tasks.
Previous commercial IT experience is not essential.

We place significant value on candidates who have balanced their studies with part-time employment, particularly in busy customer service environments.
If you've worked in hospitality or retail, understand how to communicate with different people and know the importance of delivering great service, we'd love to hear from you.
 
What's on Offer?
  • Two permanent opportunities with an established Perth MSP.
  • A genuine entry point into the IT industry.
  • Exposure to a broad range of customers, systems and technologies.
  • Hands-on learning alongside experienced IT professionals.
  • The opportunity to build skills across infrastructure, cloud, networking and IT support.
  • A collaborative, customer-focused working environment.
  • A solid foundation for long-term career progression within the technology industry.
  • Convenient location, ideal for candidates living South of the River.

job.title: P25 Radio Network Operations Engineer
job.description:
About the role:
We are seeking an experienced Level 3 Operations Engineer to support a major radio network serving a Tier 1 mining customer. You will be the senior technical escalation point between the network operations centre (NOCC) and field teams. When a fault is complex or systemic, you find the root cause and fix it.

This is not an RF design role. This is hands-on operation and sustainment of live Motorola radio networks: core and network management servers, Windows and Active Directory infrastructure, IP and transmission networks, dispatch consoles and voice logging. You'll need to understand how these layers work together as one system, and you'll need real experience on Motorola radio platforms to be considered for this SME-level position.
  • Brisbane based
  • Monday to Friday, 40 hours per week, with an afterhours on call roster
  • Permanent full-time or long-term contract opportunities available
    • Contract: $715/day incl. super (roughly $172k annual package based on 48 working weeks)
    • Permanent: up to $145k + super, depending on skill and experience
What you'll be doing:
Operations and escalation
  • Act as the Level 3 escalation point for NOCC staff and field engineers on complex or systemic faults
  • Own incidents through to root cause and resolution, and escalate customer-impacting issues to engineering with clear evidence
  • Participate in the after-hours on-call roster and support after-hours planned maintenance and upgrades
Systems and network
  • Support and maintain Motorola radio networks (ASTRO 25 P25, Dimetra, MOTOTRBO), including central and remote sites, network management systems, dispatch consoles and voice logging
  • Administer the Windows Server, Active Directory and server hardware that the radio network depends on
  • Configure, maintain and troubleshoot IP networks, LAN/WAN, routers, switches and firewalls
  • Support the microwave and MUX transmission that carries radio services, and understand how it affects the system end to end
Engineering and delivery
  • Support upgrades, integration, testing and certification activities
  • Make sure installations and configurations meet documentation and quality standards, and keep as-built documentation current
  • Develop procedures and work instructions for operations and support teams
  • Work with operations, field engineers, project teams, customers and vendors, and represent operational engineering in vendor performance issues
  • Mentor junior technical staff
  • Travel to customer sites as required
What you'll need to be successful in the role:
  • Full Australian working rights (no relocation assistance or visa sponsorship)
  • Hands-on experience supporting Motorola ASTRO 25 (P25), Dimetra (TETRA) or MOTOTRBO (DMR) in an operations, sustainment or integration role. We are looking for 3+ years on at least one of these platforms
  • Strong Windows Server and Active Directory experience (2016/2019), including server hardware and software maintenance
  • Strong IP networking experience across LAN/WAN, routers and switches
  • Proven Level 3 or SME fault finding on complex multi-site communications systems, ideally in a NOC or communications operations environment
  • A clear understanding of how servers, networks, transmission and radio fit together as one system
Highly desirable
  • CCNA/CCNP, plus Cisco or Juniper experience
  • Microwave and MUX distribution experience
  • MCC7500 console experience
  • Public safety grade encryption and key management
  • Network security: firewalls, intrusion detection, antivirus
  • VMware, Linux or SQL 
  • Tertiary qualifications in electronics or computer systems engineering (or equivalent industry experience)

job.title: FMS Product Technical Support
job.description:
About the role:
Join the Technology & Autonomy Division at a global Tier 1 Mining & Energy organisation, to support their bespoke fleet management system (FMS), ensuring the applications uptime, reliability and performance.

Act as the critical technical bridge between product development teams and mine site operations. You will look after the servers, databases and core services behind the system, making sure it is available around the clock, while working directly with everyone from operators through to site leadership. You'll troubleshoot complex backend issues, run software deployments and releases, and drive continuous improvement in how the system performs.

This opportunity is particularly suited to a Linux or DevOps focused support engineer with mining or heavy industry experience, who is comfortable supporting mission critical production systems and can explain technical issues clearly to non-technical people.
  • 12 month contract + extensions
  • Up to $75/hr + Super, depending on experience
  • This is currently a site-based role, but will soon transition back to a Perth operations environment
  • Pilbara site: 8 days on, 6 off B2B 7 nights on, 7 off. 12 hour shifts.
  • Perth based (once the team transitions back to CBD office): 8/8 roster of 4 days, 4 nights, 8 off. 12 hour shifts.
  • Work with cutting edge mining technology alongside product, software and platform engineering teams
What You'll Be Doing:
  • Manage and maintain the technical infrastructure of the fleet management system, including servers, virtual machines, databases and core services.
  • Monitor system performance using Grafana dashboards, identify bottlenecks and implement improvements.
  • Deploy software releases using Octopus Deploy and manage artifact repositories through Artifactory.
  • Perform proactive maintenance, including service restarts, cache management and preventive measures to avoid system degradation.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve complex backend issues such as database performance problems, memory leaks and service failures, using SSH and command line tools.
  • Configure and maintain application endpoints, including field hardware and workstations.
  • Manage technical integrations with OEM systems and external platforms.
  • Develop automation scripts, deployment procedures and custom tools to reduce manual work.
  • Implement monitoring, alerting and automated response procedures for critical system events.
  • Coordinate deployments and system changes during maintenance windows with minimal disruption to mining operations.
  • Manage backup, disaster recovery and high availability solutions.
  • Troubleshoot connectivity and integration issues at protocol level, and coordinate with vendors on updates, patches and escalated issues.
  • Maintain technical documentation, including runbooks, integration specifications, network diagrams and troubleshooting procedures.
What You'll Need to Be Successful:
  • Full Australian working rights & be based in Perth – this position offers NO form of Visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications or a related field, or a trade qualification or equivalent mining technology experience.
  • 2+ years in a technical role within mining, resources or heavy industry, including experience in remote site environments, ideally supporting mining technology systems (FMS, dispatch, automation)
  • Hands-on Linux system administration (RHEL, Ubuntu or CentOS).
  • Scripting experience in Python (basic), Bash or PowerShell, plus SQL.
  • Solid TCP/IP networking fundamentals and troubleshooting skills, with experience in industrial networks and communications systems.
  • Experience with configuration management and deployment tools such as Octopus Deploy or Ansible, and Docker containers (Swarm or OpenShift).
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to work independently and explain technical issues to engineers, vendors and site personnel.
  • Experience with the following will be highly regarded:
  • Fleet management systems (MineStar, FrontRunner, Modular Mining)
  • Autonomous haulage systems
  • OT/IT cybersecurity
  • Node JS/React
  • Certifications such as CCNA, Red Hat or VMware

job.title: Lead Project Engineer - Collision Avoidance Systems
job.description:

About the role:
You'll sit at the centre of a newly formed Collision Avoidance team, coordinating between engineering, project, product, and site stakeholders internally, and one external vendor delivering into an internal software platform.
This is a coordination and leadership role, not hands-on engineering. You'll be the person who keeps requirements, decisions, and deliverables aligned and traceable across the full project lifecycle, managing engineering deliverables through to sign-off and working daily between engineers, developers, and stakeholders.
  • Rate: Up to $125/hr + super, based on skill and experience
  • Contract: 12 months rolling + extensions based on performance
  • Location: Perth CBD + WFH
  • Travel: Potential for interstate + overseas vendor visits

What you'll be doing:
  • Act as the primary coordination interface between external vendors, engineering teams, project team, product team, and site personnel
  • Manage and track engineering deliverables across the project lifecycle, securing engineering sign-off on designs and related artefacts
  • Support coordination of technical interactions with external vendors, including requirements clarification, design discussions, and technical queries and follow-ups
  • Ensure outputs from technical sessions are documented, actionable, and tracked to closure
  • Maintain visibility of vendor inputs, assumptions, and responses
  • Translate engineering intent (requirements, behaviours, constraints) into clear and structured communication for Project, Site, and Vendor stakeholders
  • Coordinate and track progress of engineering artefacts (e.g. requirements, design, and related technical outputs) across the product lifecycle
  • Work daily between engineers, developers, and stakeholders to keep deliverables moving and aligned
  • Ensure that deviations, clarifications, assumptions, and key decisions are captured and documented, communicated to relevant stakeholders, and tracked for follow-up where required
  • Highlight gaps, inconsistencies, or risks in artefact alignment to appropriate stakeholders

What you'll need to be successful in the role:
  • Full Australian working rights - no Visa sponsorship or relocation assistance provided
  • 8+ years' experience in delivering complex systems or products
  • Engineering membership (e.g. Engineers Australia or equivalent) to support formal design sign-off
  • Demonstrated experience managing technical stakeholder relationships across engineering, product delivery teams, operations, and external vendors in a multi-disciplinary environment
  • Strong background in software engineering, systems engineering, systems integration, or hardware-integrated development
  • Knowledge of autonomous mining systems, collision avoidance technologies, and safety-critical operational systems
  • Proven experience working through product development lifecycle, delivering software and hardware to customers
  • Familiarity with ISO 21815, and with ISO 61508-aligned development environments (e.g. ISO26262, EN51708)

Why this role stands out:
  • Greenfield project definition phase, so you're shaping how this team operates from the start
  • Newly established team with clear direction and a genuinely positive culture
  • Significant stakeholder exposure and real ownership of a major vendor relationship
  • No FIFO. No mine site travel expected, occasional interstate or overseas vendor workshops possible
  • Reports directly to the Engineering Manager, working alongside a close-knit Collision Avoidance team
